_about: Curated, evidence-backed facts for the v2 knowledge graph. Written once from the dataset and reviewed by a person. Every evidence quote must appear verbatim in its source document (FNx = field note, Rx = research snippet, Cxx = case study problem + measured ROI). The loader refuses to start if a quote cannot be found. 'indicators' and 'glossary' are analyst mappings / plain-language labels, not evidence.

synonym_overrides._why: v2-only corrections to hr_knowledge.json synonyms. 'financial turnover risk' describes the cost of staff turnover (e.g. 'EUR 1.8M in annual financial turnover risk driven by Weak Middle Management'), not a missing CFO dashboard.

request_keywords._why: Analyst mapping from everyday words in a client's request to catalog actions (used by the request checker, not evidence). Matching is deterministic; the longest matching phrase wins.

audiences._why: Who reads the brief. The facts, numbers and sources are identical for every reader; only order, vocabulary and emphasis change.

hr.label: HR Manager
order: What to do, in what order
What we will not do, and why
hr.guidance: The reader is the HR manager who will run the plan. Use HR words they know (employer brand, EVP, time to hire, onboarding, candidate experience). Focus on what to do first, for which sites or teams, what each step needs, and what to measure.

cfo.label: CFO
order: What to do, in what order
What we will not do, and why
cfo.guidance: The reader is the CFO. Lead with money: cost, yearly benefit, conservative case, payback, and what is auditable. Translate every HR term into its business or money effect. Mention spend that is avoided or stopped.

board.label: Board members / Stakeholders
order: What to do, in what order
What we will not do, and why
board.guidance: The readers are board members and stakeholders. Be strategic and brief: the main risk, the decision needed, the order of the plan, and what is protected. No jargon.

say_do_gap: What the company promises candidates is not what employees experience.
reputation_variance: Some sites or countries are rated much worse than others, and nobody manages the difference.
evp_credibility: The employer value proposition (EVP) - why someone should work here - is not credible to candidates or staff.
portal_friction: Candidates start applying on the careers site but give up before submitting.
generic_jds: Job descriptions are boilerplate and don't speak to the people the company wants to hire.
slow_hiring: Filling a role takes too many days, so good candidates go elsewhere.
agency_dependency: Too many roles are filled by expensive temporary agencies.
candidate_feedback_gap: The company does not hear from candidates about interviews and career days.
low_social_reach: Company posts reach and engage very few people.
manual_tracking: HR tracks reviews and posts by hand, which costs hours and hides patterns.
organic_ambassadors: Some employees already share the company spontaneously - an asset to build on.
early_attrition: Too many people quit in their first months.
weak_middle_management: Team managers lack coaching or support, and employees feel it.
career_opacity: People cannot see how to get promoted or grow.
burnout: Workload or schedules are not sustainable.
compensation: Salary and benefits compared to the market.
shift_scheduling: Shift and weekend rosters are unpredictable (relevant for retail stores).
cfo_visibility_gap: No financial proof for the board
HR cannot show the CFO the money impact of employer-brand work.

actions.reputation_audit: Review all public ratings (Glassdoor, Indeed, Google) site by site to see where and why reputation differs.
actions.internal_listening_360: Ask employees, in a structured and anonymous way, how their managers, workload and growth really are.
actions.portal_ux_audit: Test the careers site the way candidates use it (often on a phone) to find exactly where they give up.
actions.persona_calibration: Define who the target candidates are and what they actually care about, cohort by cohort.
actions.candidate_feedback_digitization: Replace paper or ad-hoc feedback with a short digital survey after interviews and career days.
actions.manager_coaching: Train and coach middle managers, starting with the teams where scores are worst.
actions.career_framework: Publish clear levels and promotion criteria so people can see how to grow.
actions.evp_realignment: Rewrite the employer promise so it matches what employees really experience.
actions.board_risk_dashboard: Give the board and CFO a dashboard that shows employer-brand impact in euros.
actions.mobile_fast_apply: Offer a short mobile application (about a minute, no account needed).
actions.persona_aligned_jds: Rewrite job ads for each target group, showing the benefits that group values.
actions.technical_storytelling: Let engineers publish real technical stories on professional networks.
actions.retail_shift_rotation: Introduce predictable weekend shift rotations in stores.
actions.ambassador_selection: Select and enable employees who want to share the company story.
actions.ambassador_tracking: Track ambassador posts and reach automatically instead of in spreadsheets.
actions.compensation_review: Benchmark and adjust pay against the market.

terms.root cause: A problem that drives other problems. Fixing it removes symptoms further down the chain.
terms.symptom: A problem that is mostly a consequence of other problems. It improves when its causes are fixed.
terms.standalone problem: A real problem that is not linked to the others in the evidence. It needs its own fix.
terms.readiness gate: A safety check: ambassador and amplification actions wait until internal trust problems are fixed.
terms.say-do gap: The distance between what the company promises in recruiting and what employees report in reviews.
terms.EVP: Employer Value Proposition: the reasons the company gives for why someone should work there.
terms.EMV: Earned Media Value: what organic reach would have cost as paid advertising.
terms.DEMATEL: A standard method that scores how much each problem drives or is driven by the others, from the cause-effect links.
terms.precedent: A real case study from the dataset where a similar company had a similar problem and measured the result.
terms.peer benchmark: The sector average for companies like this client.
